o.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (söylemek, “to speak”). Cognate with Turkish söylemek.

From məqsədə (“to the purpose”) (dative case of məqsəd) + uyğun (“fit, suitable”).
Likely a calque of Russian целесообра́зный (celesoobráznyj).
Borrowed from Classical Persian نِسْیَه (nisya), from Arabic نَسِيئَة (nasīʔa).
Borrowed from Russian фармакопея (farmakopeja). Ultimately from Ancient Greek φαρμακοποιία (pharmakopoiía).
